name: St. Vera of the Unread Inbox
invocation: when the number will not go down.
blurb: Vera kept the ledger of every message she meant to answer. She is depicted holding the envelope that multiplies, and is the patron of anyone who has declared inbox bankruptcy and quietly filed for it again.

name: St. Odile of the Last Two Percent
invocation: the charger being in the other bag.
blurb: Odile walked forty days across the airport and her phone did not die until the very last gate. Carry her when the boarding pass is the only thing between you and the desk.
feastDay: Feast day: whenever you find a plug

name: St. Bartholomew of the Buttered Side Down
blurb: Bartholomew was martyred by gravity at approximately eight in the morning. He is shown with the falling toast, and is petitioned by all who have watched something small and important rotate exactly once.

name: St. Junia of the Unpaired Sock
invocation: Invoked at the bottom of the basket,
where the other one is not.
blurb: Junia searched every drum of every machine and found only one of each. Hers is the quiet patience of a household where nothing is lost, exactly, and nothing can be found.

name: St. Cassian of the Reply-All
blurb: Cassian meant it for one person. Four hundred and eleven received it. He is the patron of the cold flush, the undo window, and the sentence you would give a year of your life to recall.

name: St. Marguerite of the Spinning Wheel
invocation: the document having not been saved.
blurb: Marguerite watched the wheel turn for three days and did not force-quit. She is the patron of the unsaved draft, the beachball, and all who still believe the application will come back.

name: St. Aldous of the Forgotten Password
blurb: Aldous knew the answer to his security question and it was no longer true. He guards the padlock of asterisks and intercedes for everyone who has reset a password to the one they were already using.
feastDay: Feast day: try again in 30 minutes

name: St. Fenwick of the Untraceable Smell
invocation: Invoked on the third day of searching,
the fridge having been emptied twice.
blurb: Fenwick removed every shelf, sniffed every jar, and never found it. He is depicted with the open refrigerator, and is the patron of a house where something has happened somewhere.
feastDay: Feast day: it's gone now, isn't it
